clue.text: Landed gentry with a certain amount of paper on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts something inside the steamship letters, so on signals a container here

parts.note: on board means aboard a steamship, abbreviated SS, whose two letters wrap round the rest
a quire is a set measure of paper, twenty-four or twenty-five sheets

explanation.surface: Country landowners are carrying a ream of paperwork aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention of putting a piece between S and S, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Country gentlemen who own estates are the traditional landowning class, plural to match gentry.

clue.text: Catches up with an undoubtedly tough guy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for catches is read from bottom to top

parts.note: catches, as a verb, means traps

explanation.surface: Someone catching up with a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the word from the bottom, so the trap word is turned round before AN is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of ancient Sparta were famed for hardiness, so the word names a person of great endurance and austerity.

clue.text: Not all adult radio plays are extreme

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Grown-up radio drama is going too far.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'plays are extreme' as the definition, but 'plays are' only links the hidden run to the definition: the answer means extreme alone.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes views or measures going far beyond the moderate, a synonym of extreme.

clue.text: Fleet for which the monarch paid out

parts.note: R stands for Rex or Regina, king or queen

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of paid are put out of order

explanation.surface: A navy that the king funded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy, which suits the monarch; here it is the adjective meaning swift, and 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift or quick-moving, a synonym.

clue.text: Think perhaps American coppers should go in a group

indicators.note: these words tell us that one set of letters is to be placed inside another word

parts.note: a sect is a group sharing a belief
P stands for pence, coins once made of copper

explanation.surface: Perhaps US police officers ought to join a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police but gives P, pennies. 'Think perhaps' fits because suspecting is one way of thinking something.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect is to believe something likely without proof, an example of thinking.

clue.text: State of egg — a1 or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the figure 1 is read as the letter I, giving A and I

explanation.surface: A top-quality egg, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a1' looks like first-class, but the 1 is read as I to supply letters for the mix of EGG, A, I and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the south-east, named after King George II.

clue.text: Sound first-rate purchase. The last word!

indicators.note: Sound tells us the answer is spoken like the phrase that follows

parts.note: a first-rate purchase is a good buy

explanation.surface: Praising a sound bargain, then signing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective praising the purchase but signals that GOOD BUY is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Farewell is said as the final word when parting, hence a valediction.

clue.text: Intimidating — and all through a fly

parts.note: over can mean throughout, as in all over the place
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Frightening, as a fly buzzes around everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an insect but is the verb, matching WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring awe that subdues someone is a form of cowing or frightening.

clue.text: The newly-wed will take only a little water in a restaurant

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it, so it is a container

parts.note: a groom is a newly married man
a rill is a small stream, just a little water

explanation.surface: A bridegroom drinks just a sip of water at a dinner out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery that specialises in grilled food is a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: The player finds a considerable number lock

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A musician discovers a large number lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a fastening but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who plays roles on stage is a player in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: An advisory word concerning hors d'oeuvres

parts.note: a tip is a word of advice
as to means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A suggestion about starters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian first course of cold meats and olives is the equivalent of starters served before a meal.

clue.text: The writer will find a quarter back labour

parts.note: E is east, one of the four compass quarters

indicators.note: back means the word for labour is read in reverse

parts.note: toil means hard labour

explanation.surface: An author discovers that some of the work has gone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal on the word for labour; 'a quarter' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. or George, either is a famous author with this surname.

clue.text: Beginning to walk like a duck? Nonsense!

indicators.note: Beginning picks the opening letter of the word to

parts.note: ducks famously move with a waddle

explanation.surface: Learning to walk with a duck's gait? Rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to walk' reads as a toddler's first steps, but 'Beginning' acts on 'to' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly talk or rubbish is a synonym for nonsense, an informal British word.

clue.text: Liberal arrangement to assist the blind

definitions.note: the definition describes a purpose; the answer is the reading system that serves it

indicators.note: an arrangement of the letters means they are reordered

explanation.surface: A Liberal political scheme helping sightless people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a party but is just the fodder; 'arrangement' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised-dot writing system lets sightless people read by touch.

clue.text: Keep going after modern urban development

indicators.note: going after places the word for keep behind the word for modern

parts.note: new means modern
a keep is the stronghold of a castle

explanation.surface: Keep up with the latest town planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep going' reads as an instruction to continue; 'Keep' is the noun, a fortified tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in north-east England, an urban settlement that grew around its fortress.

clue.text: A one-sided token in troubled times

definitions.text: A one-sided token in troubled times

parts.words: A one-sided token in troubled times
parts.note: a flower badge worn by one faction, Yorkshire's, during the Wars of the Roses in fifteenth-century England

explanation.surface: A partisan symbol during a period of unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses were English civil wars between York and Lancaster, each side with a rose emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The badge of the House of York was the emblem of one side in those civil wars.

clue.text: Temperate but bent — isn't a convert

indicators.note: convert means change, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Moderate yet crooked, someone who has not changed faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' looks like a noun for a new believer but is a verb rearranging BENT ISNT A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who refrains from alcohol is moderate in habits.

clue.text: Does some evening work for clubs

definitions.meaning: smooths clothes flat with a hot appliance, evening meaning making even

explanation.surface: Puts in overtime for the golfing society.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing garments smooths them, and in golf the metal-headed clubs share the name.

clue.text: A music man who could give great joy

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur, an English composer and Master of the Queen's Music

explanation.surface: A musician who brings happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur was a twentieth-century English composer, and the common noun means perfect happiness.

clue.text: Take responsibility on occasion for a small charge

definitions.text: Take responsibility on occasion for a small charge

parts.words: Take responsibility on occasion for a small charge
parts.note: a small charge looks like a modest fee but is a little child in one's care for an evening

explanation.surface: Accept liability now and then for a minor fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding someone's child while the parents are out means looking after a young ward temporarily.

clue.text: William's backers, getting a sign, wander in

indicators.note: in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: an omen is a sign of the future
to range is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: King William's supporters receive a portent and stroll in.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Orange, King William III, is honoured by the Protestant Orange Order in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order are supporters of William of Orange.

clue.text: Musical drama the heartless act

parts.note: an opera is a sung drama

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cruel musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like cruelty but strips the H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To act can mean to function or work, as a machine or surgeon does.

clue.text: A fool suffers attacks

parts.note: an ass is a fool
ails means is unwell or suffers

explanation.surface: A fool is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault someone violently or verbally is to attack them.

clue.text: Change we yearn for when Christmas is over

indicators.note: Change tells us to alter the order of the letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Wanting a fresh start after the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges WE YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: The calendar turns from one twelvemonth to the next a week after December 25th.

clue.text: A worker has to hurry about five for home

parts.note: a worker bee

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the next piece

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning hurry
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An employee must rush back for dinner around five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is the crossword convention for a bee; 'about' puts V inside HIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hive is where bees live, their dwelling.

clue.text: Frivolous demonstration taking in everyone

indicators.note: taking in means one word contains the other

parts.note: a show is a demonstration
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A trivial display involving the whole crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth of thought is being superficial, close to frivolous.

clue.text: Moving article on prison

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Emotional report about a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and about, in motion, is a sense of moving.

clue.text: Little Letitia races into the meadow

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a ley is a meadow or pasture
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is a motorcycle race series on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A girl dashes into the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a pet form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A short familiar form of the girl's name, little meaning a diminutive.

clue.text: Articulated part of a wheel

definitions.meaning: uttered words, the past tense of talk
a rod running from hub to rim

explanation.surface: A jointed component of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttered words is the past of talk, and a wheel's radial rod shares the spelling.

clue.text: Well-known Greek's child left in a lift

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition

indicators.note: in means the second group is placed inside the first

parts.note: a rise is a lift
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A famous Greek's youngster left in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' suggests an elevator but is a noun; 'in' puts the child and left together inside A plus the word for lift.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander, is famous.

clue.text: Odd letters may be written to gain support

indicators.note: Odd suggests the letters are in a strange order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange characters written to win backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' reads as odd-numbered letters, but it signals rearranging LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of legs and a bar holding up a table top is a support.

clue.text: This could well cause some misting

definitions.text: This could well cause some misting

parts.words: This could well cause some misting
parts.note: a device that sends out a fine mist of liquid, as on plants or paint

explanation.surface: Something likely to fog things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser or nozzle device that ejects fine droplets produces a mist.
